canonical_name: pyribs -- 'Pyribs: A Bare-Bones Python Library for Quality Diversity Optimization' (Tjanaka, Bryon and Fontaine, Matthew C and Lee, David H and Zhang, Yulun and Balam, Nivedit Reddy and Dennler, Nathaniel and Garlanka, Sujay S and Klapsis, Nikitas Dimitri and Nikolaidis, Stefanos; ICAROS Lab, University of Southern California; 2020-2026, GECCO 2023 paper)
aliases: RIBS (Rapid Illumination of Behavior Space framework)
lineage: README: implements the 'Rapid Illumination of Behavior Space (RIBS)' framework; adopts the ask-tell interface from pycma ('Users of pycma will be familiar with the ask-tell interface (which pyribs adopted)'); 'We thank Amy K. Hoover and Julian Togelius for their contributions deriving the CMA-ME algorithm'; package skeleton from Cookiecutter audreyr/cookiecutter-pypackage. README 'Additional QD Libraries' names peers QDax, qdpy, sferes (not predecessors). Algorithms implemented and their sources are tabulated in docs/supported-algorithms.md (MAP-Elites Mouret 2015; CVT-MAP-Elites Vassiliades 2018; CMA-ME Fontaine 2020; CMA-MEGA/OMG-MEGA Fontaine 2021; CMA-MAE Fontaine 2023; DDS Lee 2024; DMS Tjanaka 2026; BOP-Elites Kent 2024; Novelty Search/NSLC Lehman 2011; QDAIF, QDHF). HISTORY.md tracks releases back through 0.x. || main loop (reader, from the code): The user loop calls Scheduler.ask(), which concatenates each emitter's ask() (GaussianEmitter: random archive elites plus Gaussian noise; EvolutionStrategyEmitter: samples from an internal CMA-ES), the user evaluates objectives and measures, then Scheduler.tell() inserts the batch into the archive (GridArchive.add: measure -> cell index, keep the per-cell argmax objective only if it exceeds the cell's threshold, returning a status/value add_info) and hands each emitter its slice of solutions and add_info so the emitter can rank, adapt its distribution and possibly restart from a sampled elite.

entry_points: ribs/schedulers/_scheduler.py Scheduler (ask() concatenates each emitter's ask(); tell() validates data, adds the batch to archive (and optional result_archive) via _add_to_archives, then slices add_info back to each emitter's tell())

ribs/archives/_grid_archive.py GridArchive.add (index_of maps measures to grid cells; can_insert = objective > cell threshold; per-cell argmax via numpy_groupies aggregate; threshold update per Fontaine 2023 when learning_rate/threshold_min set, otherwise vanilla MAP-Elites replacement; returns status/value add_info)
ribs/archives/_cvt_archive.py CVTArchive + k_means_centroids (CVT-MAP-Elites archive: cells are nearest centroids; centroids from sklearn k_means on uniform samples)
ribs/archives/_archive_base.py ArchiveBase (abstract add/add_single/retrieve/sample_elites/data interface all archives implement)

ribs/emitters/_evolution_strategy_emitter.py EvolutionStrategyEmitter (CMA-ME emitter: ask() samples from self._opt (CMA-ES etc. in ribs/emitters/opt); tell() ranks via ranker, selects parents by 'mu' or 'filter', updates ES, restarts from a random archive elite when stopped or no improvement)
ribs/emitters/_gaussian_emitter.py GaussianEmitter.ask (MAP-Elites emitter: sample elites from archive and add Gaussian noise; x0 / initial_solutions when archive empty)
ribs/emitters/_iso_line_emitter.py IsoLineEmitter and ribs/emitters/operators/_iso_line.py (MAP-Elites (line) variation operator)
ribs/emitters/_emitter_base.py EmitterBase (ask/tell/ask_dqd/tell_dqd abstract interface); ribs/emitters/rankers.py (ranking criteria e.g. TwoStageImprovementRanker used by CMA-ME)

example.command: README 'Usage' Python snippet: GridArchive(solution_dim=10, dims=[20, 20], ranges=[(-1, 1), (-1, 1)]); three EvolutionStrategyEmitter(archive, x0=[0.0]*10, sigma0=0.1, batch_size=36); Scheduler(archive, emitters); 1000 iterations of scheduler.ask() / scheduler.tell(objectives, measures). Smallest shell commands: python -c "import ribs; print(ribs.__version__)" (README) and python sphere.py map_elites (examples/sphere.py docstring).
example.input: 10-D negative Sphere function: objectives = -np.sum(np.square(solutions), axis=1); measures = solutions[:, :2]; 3 emitters x batch 36 = 108 solutions per iteration for 1000 iterations
example.output: A populated GridArchive (20x20 cells of best solutions per measure cell) visualised with ribs.visualize.grid_archive_heatmap(archive); README shows readme_assets/sphere_heatmap.png

human_capability_summary.built_to: README: 'A bare-bones Python library for quality diversity (QD) optimization. Pyribs implements the highly modular Rapid Illumination of Behavior Space (RIBS) framework for QD optimization', and is 'the official implementation of' CMA-ME, CMA-MEGA, CMA-MAE, scalable CMA-MAE and Discount Model Search (DMS).
human_capability_summary.pressure: README BibTeX abstract: 'we believe the QD community faces two challenges: developing a framework to represent the field's growing array of algorithms, and implementing that framework in software that supports a range of researchers and practitioners'; README: 'like pycma, pyribs focuses on optimizing fixed-dimensional continuous domains. Focusing on this one commonly-occurring problem allows us to optimize the library for performance as well as ease of use.'
human_capability_summary.success_means: README does not state a numeric metric; it frames success as the three principles 'Simple', 'Flexible', 'Accessible' and the ability to 'compose a large number of QD algorithms' by interchanging archive/emitter/scheduler; the code tracks archive stats (ArchiveStats, QD score via qd_score_offset, ribs/archives/_cqd_score.py) and the examples visualise archive heatmaps.
